question: Can Temporal v0.1 represent a legal interval whose start and end are specified to the minute with a legally meaningful timezone?

official_rule.rule: The real-time closure enters into force at 24:00 UTC on the day of decision and lasts 14 days, after which it automatically ceases at midnight UTC.

boundary_adversaries.why: The local calendar date has begun but the closure has not yet started.
The exact start boundary is inclusive.
The source expressly includes the final minute through 00:59 Swedish time.
The EU rule ceases the closure at midnight UTC, equal to 01:00 CET.

v0_1_probe.schema_problem: normalized_date and absolute trigger date are format=date, not date-time.
v0_1_probe.resolver_problem: resolver.py parses legal/query time through datetime.date.fromisoformat and therefore cannot compare offset-aware instants.

forbidden_inferences: The closure was active for the entire calendar date 18 February 2025.
The closure was active for the entire calendar date 4 March 2025.
Swedish local time can be dropped without changing the legal interval.
A date-only Temporal assertion is an acceptable approximation of an exact official time boundary.
The spatial closure should own these times because it is a spatial rule.
